transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-01-18
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Jenna (Redwood CSM); Asha (Procurement), Luis (Security), Daniel (VP Eng), Maya (Legal)

Summary (auto): Quick procurement gating + KMS/residency preflight. Customer requests conditional approval path so procurement can clear pilot pending DPA redlines and KMS keying model. Discussed hosted vs dedicated economics, egress fees, auditability, and SSO/KMS integration.

--- Transcript Body ---
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we wanted to run through the conditional approval playbook, and make sure the KMS and residency questions are clear before procurement raises the PO.
[00:18] Asha: Yeah, thanks Sofia. Quick context, procurement's got a conditional approval lane — they want legal and security signoff on the non-negotiables before we go to finance.
[00:30] Maya: hi all, Maya from legal. we have a handful of DPA/MSA items. Most important for us is auditable access to keys, indemnity carve-outs, and clarity on sub-processors and data location. can you explain the KMS options again?
[00:47] Marco: Sure, so Redwood supports three patterns: managed KMS (we hold keys in our KMS), customer-managed cloud KMS (bring-your-own-key in AWS KMS/GCP KMS/Azure Key Vault), and HSM-backed on-premamento for private deployments. there's also an option for encrypted-at-rest with zero-knowledge key wrapping — sorry, zero-trust key wrap.
[01:10] Luis: Quick q — if we bring our own KMS, does Redwood ever see plaintext keys or key material?
[01:17] Marco: No. When you BYOK the keys, the key material stays within your KMS; Redwood receives just an encrypted wrap token and uses KMS APIs (encrypt/decrypt calls) for ephemeral operations. we don't persist plaintext keys. there is a small nuance for hosted low-latency where we cache a wrapping token in memory — we call that KV cache but I sometimes hear it as KV cash — it's ephemeral and never written to disk.
[01:40] Daniel: And latency impact? we have interactive use-cases so 50-100ms tail latency matters. if we route key calls cross-region that kills SLOs.
[01:50] Marco: Right — two options: colocate KMS in same cloud region and route via private VPC peering, or use dedicated Redwood capacity in the same region (dedicated pools) to reduce roundtrips. we can also recommend minimal key-use design where only session tokens are used for per-request verification.
[02:10] Asha: On procurement side, we need data residency guarantees for EU customers and an audit log retention of 7 years for some regulated lines. does Redwood support different retention windows per route/account?
[02:22] Jenna: Yes. We can configure retention per-customer and per-route. our console stores audit logs and you can export to your SIEM; retention can be 90 days by default but enterprise tiers allow custom retention, we also have an archival option. note: long-term retention may have cost/egress implications.
[02:39] Maya: egress fees. procurement wants a clear summary of likely egress costs for the pilot and what triggers extra fees.
[02:47] Sofia: We'll include a cost projection in the pricing worksheet — Host vs Dedicated vs Private will have different egress profiles. for private on-prem, egress is a non-issue. for hosted API, repeated embedding calls can be the main driver.
[03:00] Luis: Security-wise, SOC2 and ISO look good on the vendor page, but we need evidence — certs, and also to understand internal access controls: RBAC, SSO, session recording, and who can call admin APIs.
[03:12] Jenna: I'll share the SOC2 Type II report and our ISO27001 cert. RBAC is role-based in the console with fine-grained API keys and token-scoped roles; we support SAML 2.0/SSO and SCIM provisioning.
[03:27] Daniel: Can we get a short diagram of the SAML flow + how tokens map to jobs in Redwood? we have to show it to infra.
[03:35] Marco: absolutely, i'll draw up the SAML->token flow and how it maps to route-level RBAC. expect that in the KMS doc.
[03:42] [crosstalk] Asha: for procurement timeline — if legal provides initial redlines, how fast can finance clear a pilot?
[03:48] Sofia: Typically conditioned approvals take 7-14 days after redlines depending on counterparty intake. if DPA items are mostly standard, we can do a 30-60 day pilot with conditional PO and then finalize MSA after pilot success.
[04:04] Maya: Our key concerns: indemnity caps, audit rights, data residency clauses, subprocessor list, and export controls. Also, can you tell me about your access logs for who queried what model and when?
[04:18] Jenna: We surface per-token logs and per-request metadata in the console, and we can push logs to your S3 or GCS with encryption. logs include request id, model variant, timestamps, and route — we redact PII by default but we can configure raw payload retention under an enterprise contract.
[04:37] Luis: is there an eDiscovery or legal hold capability? we have regulatory cases where we need immutable retention.
[04:44] Marco: We have an archive + WORM-like bucket export that serves that purpose; again that tends to be enterprise add-on because of storage/retention costs.
[04:58] Daniel: about pricing approvals — procurement wants three options: minimal hosted (pay-as-you-go), reserved dedicated (monthly/commit), and private on-prem license. can you sketch cost tradeoffs?
[05:10] Sofia: Sure. Hosted lowest op-ex to start but higher unit cost. Dedicated has higher commit but reduces per-token unit cost by ~30-45% for steady throughput. Private is license plus support, highest up-front but lowest per-unit and gives full data control. we'll send a worksheet.
[05:27] Asha: For conditional approval we need a Pilot SOW: objectives, acceptance criteria, token caps, and exit criteria. can Redwood support a failover policy if we observe quality regressions during pilot?
[05:40] Marco: We can bake in rollbacks and automated fallback routes — e.g., if latency > X or quality drops, fallback to smaller model or cached responses. We can also freeze model versions for the pilot.
[05:55] Maya: On DPA — are you open to adding customer audit rights for key usage and to include a clause limiting subprocessor changes without notice?
[06:05] Sofia: We're flexible. our standard DPA has a subprocessor list, 30-day notice for new subproc. We can accept a short audit window for critical customers.
[06:15] Daniel: about network connectivity — can Redwood support VPC peering and private endpoints to avoid internet egress?
[06:23] Marco: Yes, private endpoints + VPC peering are available for Dedicated and Private deployments, and hosted customers can request private link setups in supported clouds.
[06:32] Luis: Any multitenancy concerns? will tenant A ever see requests from tenant B in logs or errors?
[06:39] Marco: No cross-tenant exposure. We shard workloads logically and enforce tenant isolation at the runtime; logs are tagged and partitioned by account. occasional misattribution in transcripts aside, the system is designed to isolate.
[06:55] Asha: procurement ask — net30 payment terms but interest penalties for late payments; any minimums for pilot PO?
[07:04] Sofia: For pilots we accept smaller POs; net30 is standard but we can negotiate net45 for some enterprise customers. for reserved capacity there are minimum monthly commits.
[07:14] Maya: indemnity — we usually request mutual indemnity with carve-outs for gross negligence. does Redwood accept that?
[07:21] Sofia: Mutual indemnity with cap at fees paid in last 12 months is typical. we've done limited carve-outs for privacy breaches — we can discuss specifics in legal thread.
[07:34] Daniel: benchmarks — we want to run a short run-for-run comparing Redwood hosted vs our in-house stack for 1000 concurrent chat sessions. can Redwood provision a dedicated pool for a short window?
[07:45] Marco: Yes we can allocate a dedicated trial pool for benchmarking. we'll need expected qps and model sizes. we'll coordinate scheduling to avoid noisy neighbors.
[07:58] Luis: encryption at rest — if we use BYOK, do you support envelope encryption and customer-controlled rotation?
[08:07] Marco: Yes envelope encryption supported and rotation policies can be customer controlled. rotation still requires brief rewrap calls but we can schedule them during low traffic windows.
[08:20] Asha: is there a standard procurement checklist or external docs we can share internally?
[08:27] Jenna: I'll share a procurement playbook (pdf) that outlines SSO, KMS, SLA, pricing, and escalation paths.
[08:35] Maya: About the SLA — uptime targets, credits, and SLOs for tail latency? we need explicit call outs.
[08:44] Sofia: Our enterprise SLA covers 99.9% uptime for dedicated and private, 99.5% for hosted API. latency SLOs are documented per-model and per-region; credits are applied proportionally to the impacted route.
[08:59] Daniel: Do we get a runbook for incident escalation and postmortem access?
[09:04] Jenna: yes. we provide a dedicated escalation contact for enterprise accounts, postmortem summary, and timeline access for incidents; we can also arrange a postmortem bridge-in for critical issues.
[09:18] [15m skip simulation note — we skip routine back-and-forth to preserve time]
[24:22] Maya: on export controls — we operate with EU and a couple APAC prod regions, we need to ensure there's no transfer of regulated data outside permitted regions. how does Redwood handle cross-border processing?
[24:33] Marco: We can pin deployments to region and enforce routing policy. Smart routing will keep EU traffic in EU unless you opt-in to fallback routes. fallback to another region is only used for outages and requires customer opt-in.
[24:48] Luis: Are the fallbacks auditable? We need a log of any request that took fallback routing for compliance audits.
[24:55] Jenna: Absolutely. fallback events are logged and we can push an alerting feed.
[25:05] Asha: procurement needs to know what exceptions could delay approval — e.g., nonstandard indemnity, non-negotiable subprocessor terms, or egress cap.
[25:16] Sofia: If those show up, it usually pushes things to a legal review and takes 2-3 weeks. We try to triage high-priority items during the first week.
[25:25] Daniel: On the pilot SOW acceptance criteria — define quality metric and latency threshold. will Redwood help run evaluation harness?
[25:34] Marco: Yes, we have evaluation tooling and can run A/B tests with your golden prompts. we can store prompt sets and track regressions.
[25:45] Maya: one more legal item — for DPA we insist on a clause to notify us within 72 hours for any breach impacting our data. is that acceptable?
[25:52] Sofia: 72-hour notification for breaches is our standard industry practice; we'll confirm in the DPA.
[26:00] Asha: good. to summarize — procurement wants conditional path: pilot SOW, DPA redlines, KMS integration details, cost worksheet. if those are OK, we can get a conditional PO and start a 30-60 day pilot.
[26:15] Sofia: Great recap. we'll action items: pricing worksheet, SOW, KMS diagram, SOC2/ISO certs, DPA redline response.
[26:22] [crosstalk / short clarifications]
[26:40] Daniel: scheduling the benchmark — we have a 2-hour window on 2026-01-27 or 2026-01-29 mornings.
[26:48] Marco: i'll propose both slots and check infra capacity.
[26:54] Luis: final Q — can Redwood commit to not using customer data for model training? that's a blocking ask for us.
[27:02] Sofia: Yes. We have explicit data use opt-outs in the enterprise contract; we'll include a no-training clause for customer data in the SOW for the pilot.
[27:14] Maya: Excellent. one procedural note — legal prefers redlines via track changes on canonical MSA; we don't want to re-draft from scratch.
[27:23] Sofia: Understood. we'll send the canonical MSA and a proposed addendum for the KMS/Residency items.
[27:30] Asha: procurement will push the conditional PO after we receive the pilot SOW and cost worksheet.
[27:36] Sofia: Perfect. anything else?
[27:40] [silence]
[27:45] Sofia: ok, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the docs and next steps in the thread.
[27:52] Maya: thanks all.
[27:55] Meeting end.

Recap (auto):
- Pilot SOW required: objectives, acceptance criteria, token caps, duration (30-60d)
- DPA redlines: Maya to send non-negotiables; Redwood to produce redline response
- KMS: Marco to share integration diagram and explain envelope encryption + BYOK flow
- SLA/Certs: Jenna to share SOC2/ISO artifacts and support SLA matrix
- Benchmarks: Redwood to provision dedicated pool for run-for-run testing; Daniel to confirm slot
- Costs: Sofia to send pricing worksheet covering hosted, dedicated, private options and egress estimates

Closeout notes: Customer emphasized: no training on customer data (must be contractually enforced), 72-hour breach notification, auditability for fallback routing, and archive/WORM retention options for legal hold. Procurement indicated conditional PO will be issued once pilot SOW, pricing, and DPA redline responses are acceptable.
